title: Cosanima 1.0.0 — coordinated flag-day release
goal: Coordinate the Cosanima 1.0.0 flag-day: the brand rename, Apache-2.0 license, repo split, versioned frontend contract, and per-frontend CI land together as one release across the core and six frontend repos, and the stable surface the contract commits to is ruled here.

title: v1.0.0 coordinated tags
body: All seven repos — the cosanima core and the six frontends (cosanima-go/java/cpp/rust/ts/csharp) — release as v1.0.0 on the same flag-day, cut from green CI, using the new name, license, and repo layout.

title: cosanima --version reports 1.0.0
body: After the rename, `cosanima --version` reports 1.0.0 (the crate was 0.9.2 pre-flag-day). The version value is a release-gate, distinct from the frontend schema revision.

title: CHANGELOG committed and current
body: A CHANGELOG.md is committed in the core repo covering the 0.9 → 1.0.0 history (rename, license, split, frontend contract, CI) and is kept current; it is one of the two committed docs (with SPEC.md) required by the stable surface.

title: License sweep coordinated across seven repos
body: The parent coordinates the Apache-2.0 license sweep across the core and all six frontend repos (executed by cosanima-license) so all seven carry the identical license at v1.0.0.

title: Flag-day launch checklist green
body: A single flag-day launch checklist gates the tags: every child deliverable reaches its final phase (rename shipped, license swept, split live, validate oracle released, per-frontend CI green) before any v1.0.0 tag is cut.

title: Platform matrix declared (Windows unsupported)
body: Declare the 1.0 platform matrix: macOS and Linux are supported; Windows is explicitly unsupported for 1.0 and this stance is stated in the README and the frontend contract rather than left silent. (Ruled from the source's 'Windows: currently macOS + Linux only; 1.0 should state unsupported/support' residual gap.)

title: C++ fidelity declared best-effort
body: Formally declare in the frontend contract that C++ edges are best-effort/heuristic (tree-sitter + scope/type tracking), while Go/Java/Rust/TS/C# edges are exact (compiler type-check). The contract states the fidelity difference so consumers can rely on it. (Ruled from the source's 'C++ fidelity' residual gap.)

title: Committed SPEC.md + CHANGELOG
body: Commit both SPEC.md and CHANGELOG.md at the v1.0.0 tag and keep them current. SPEC.md is referenced constantly by AGENTS.md but is not checked in today; this closes that gap. (Ruled from the source's 'Committed SPEC.md + CHANGELOG' residual gap.)

summary: One coordinated flag-day release: rename + license + repo split + frontend contract + CI land together as 1.0.0 (source Sequence: 'Then 1.0.0 ... as the coordinated flag-day'), not incrementally.

body: No Windows support build-out for 1.0 — the stance is declared unsupported; there is no work to make Windows run.

No behavioural change to any frontend for 1.0: C++ stays heuristic/best-effort and Go/Java/Rust/TS/C# stay exact — the only new frontend-facing capability is the validate harness + versioned handshake (cosanima-frontend-interface).

No migration tooling/path for pre-1.0 `apg` installs: the install base is deliberately small and the rename is cheapest now; users re-init with cosanima rather than running an automated apg→cosanima migration.

source: SPEC-1.0.0.md's Name section named the leading candidate `anima` with alternates (telos, sophia/gnosis, lore, atlas) and flagged availability as 'required before commit'; the binding design decision is Cosanima, availability confirmed cleared. Recorded to keep the naming choice reviewable [with user].

source: SPEC-1.0.0.md uses the working placeholder `carto` throughout (carto scan, carto init, carto frontend validate, SUPPORTED_CARTO, carto-1.0, carto-rename/license/repo-split/frontend-interface/frontend-ci, carto-go/java/cpp/rust/ts/csharp); materialized as the cosanima equivalent in the parent and every child project per the binding name decision [with user].

source: SPEC-1.0.0.md's 'Residual gaps (unruled — candidate open questions)' (Windows, C++ fidelity, stable/semver surface, committed SPEC.md + CHANGELOG) is materialized as RULED stable-surface requirements + decisions (R7/D3, R8/D4, R6/D5, R9) rather than left as open questions [autonomous].

The 0.9.1/0.9.2 prerequisite (SPEC-0.9.1.md scan-unblock) shipped and the code graph is now populated, so 1.0.0 is the active target and this spec is the dogfood of the graph-native authoring loop. 0.9.1 was NOT materialized as a delivered spec (optional per scope; primary deliverable is 1.0.0) — its proof (a populated graph) is the ground this spec sits on.

The parent release spec holds the cross-cutting gates (1.0.0 version/tag, coordinated launch flag-day, CHANGELOG, license-sweep coordination, stable-surface rulings, test gate) and SpecDependsOn each child; the children own their execution scope. Requirement-to-phase placement is finalized when the plan-writer maps each requirement onto plan phases (Satisfies).
Seven v1.0.0 tags exist (core + six frontends), cut from green CI on the same flag-day.
`cosanima --version` prints 1.0.0; CHANGELOG.md + SPEC.md are committed at the tag and referenced from the README.
Every requirement in the five child specs reaches its final phase before any tag is cut (no child requirement left planned at flag-day).
Verification: `git tag v1.0.0` present on all seven repos with matching flag-day dates.
Verification: post-launch smoke — brew-install a cosanima formula, scan a real repo, and run `cosanima frontend validate` on a frontend's golden output; all succeed.

summary: Brand: Cosanima (binding). cos + anima = 'living cosmos / world-soul' (Greek kosmos 'order, world' + Latin anima 'breath, life, soul'). Availability cleared (npm, crates.io 0 crates, brew, domains cosanima.com/.dev/.ai/.io/.app); only irrelevant web hits (no software trademark pressure). GitHub-org dimension superseded by the org decision: the owning org is really-knows-ai (already existing or to be created) and the cosanima* repos (core + six frontends) plus the brew tap live under it — the earlier 'GitHub org cosanima is free' check is no longer the operative criterion. Replaces BOTH the current `apg` name and the doc's working placeholder `carto` and the doc's leading candidate `anima`.

body: source: decision-D1 recorded "Availability cleared (npm, crates.io 0 crates, brew, GitHub org, domains …)" and the earlier availability note read "GitHub org cosanima is free"; the binding org decision makes that criterion non-operative; resolution: the owning org is really-knows-ai (already existing or to be created) and the repos are the cosanima* names under it — really-knows-ai/cosanima, really-knows-ai/cosanima-{go,java,cpp,rust,ts,csharp}, brew tap really-knows-ai/cosanima; the product name stays cosanima; D1 summary updated to match (availability now lists domains/registries only, GitHub-org clause re-stated) [with user].

The stable surface is documented in SPEC.md (JSONL schema, FQN rules, DB schema, CLI flags/subcommands, tool/agent names, config.json shape, SUPPORTED_COSANIMA version-string format, .trans/ data layout), and the README + frontend contract state Windows-unsupported and C++-best-effort.

source/ruling: the user broadened the 1.0 stable surface to also include the config.json (→ cosanima/config.json) shape, the SUPPORTED_COSANIMA version-string format, and the .trans/ data layout, beyond the original 5-item set. inconsistency: R6 + Decision D5 enumerated only JSONL schema, FQN rules, DB schema, CLI flags, tool/agent names [autonomous]. resolution: R6 now enumerates the broadened set (config.json shape, SUPPORTED_COSANIMA format, .trans/ data layout added); D5 and ac-3 updated to match [with user].

title: Rust core test gate: review + harden the suite
body: The 1.0.0 release gate includes REVIEWING and HARDENING the current Rust core test suite — not merely 'must pass today'. The suite is reviewed and strengthened (coverage, robustness, correctness) as part of the release gate, then the full `cargo test` must pass before any 1.0.0 tag is cut (currently tests run only locally; source: 'Rust core test gate before any tag release (currently tests run only locally)'). This is the hardened release test gate, enforced on the flag-day checklist.

summary: The Rust core test gate is a release gate that REVIEWS and HARDENS the current Rust core test suite — strengthening it rather than merely requiring it to pass today — then requires full `cargo test` green before any 1.0.0 tag (currently tests run only locally) [with user].

body: Verification: the Rust core test suite has been reviewed and hardened (coverage/robustness strengthened), and `cargo test` is green on the core immediately before tagging (hardened test gate).

title: Core repo PR CI lane (Rust build + tests)
body: The core repo (really-knows-ai/cosanima) runs its own CI lane on every PR: `cargo build` + the full `cargo test` suite must pass. This is distinct from the per-frontend CI lanes (cosanima-frontend-ci — one native lane per frontend repo over the validate oracle) and from the tag-time hardened test gate (R10: the reviewed/hardened suite enforced on the flag-day checklist). It closes the gap where frontend CI is per-repo but the core's own PR CI lane was implicit: the core's Rust build + tests are CI-enforced on PR so the repo stays green independent of the per-frontend lanes, and the tag-time gate (R10) remains the harder, review-gated bar.

No external-contributor PR gating / contributor-onboarding automation before 1.0 — deferred to post-1.0, behind the license + DCO contributor-agreement decision (source CI/quality: 'candidate to defer to post-1.0, behind license + contrib-agreement decision'). The core's own PR CI lane (R11) and the per-frontend CI lanes (cosanima-frontend-ci) are internal repo lanes, not contribution onboarding; this non-goal was narrowed from 'No PR-check CI …' when R11 made the core's own lane explicit.

summary: The core repo's own PR CI lane (Rust build + tests on every PR, R11) is in scope for 1.0 — the core's per-repo lane was implicit and is now explicit. It is distinct from the per-frontend CI lanes (cosanima-frontend-ci) and from the tag-time hardened test gate (R10). Non-goal ng-2 is narrowed accordingly: external-contributor PR gating / contributor-onboarding automation remains deferred post-1.0 behind the DCO decision; internal repo lanes (core + frontends) are not that deferred item. [with user]

body: source: the user directed a new parent requirement under quality-gates — the core repo runs its own CI lane on PR (Rust build + tests), distinct from the per-frontend CI lanes (cosanima-frontend-ci) and from the tag-time test gate (R10), closing the gap where the core's own PR CI lane was implicit. inconsistency: parent non-goal ng-2 stated 'No PR-check CI … before 1.0', which the new lane contradicts verbatim. resolution: added R11 (core repo PR CI lane) under quality-gates; narrowed ng-2 → ng-5 to the deferred item's actual intent (external-contributor PR gating / contributor-onboarding automation, behind the license + DCO decision), recording that internal repo lanes (core R11 + per-frontend lanes) are not that deferred item; added Decision D7 recording the ruling. The non-goal was re-added under id ng-5 (monotonic counter, ng-2 not reused) [with user].

title: Name the stable surface (broadened, MCP agent-facing surface)
body: Name the stable surface the 1.0 contract commits to: the unified JSONL line schema, the FQN rules, the DB (LadybugDB/parquet) schema, the CLI flags/subcommands, the `apg/config.json` → `cosanima/config.json` configuration shape, the `SUPPORTED_COSANIMA` version-string format (each frontend's declared schema range), the `.trans/` on-disk data layout (db.lbug + graph.jsonl + logs under the data dir), and — for the agent-facing surface — the MCP tool set + MCP resource names + the six agent names from cosanima-mcp (the retired opencode tool suite is NOT part of the stable surface: the `cosanima_*` opencode tool names are never shipped). Anything outside this enumerated set is not part of the stable surface for 1.0. (Broadened per the user's ruling; the tool/agent-names item now resolves to the MCP surface per cosanima-mcp, superseding the earlier reading of opencode tool names.)

summary: The stable surface is the broadened enumerated contract set: JSONL schema, FQN rules, DB schema, CLI flags/subcommands, the MCP tool set + resource names + agent names (the agent-facing surface per cosanima-mcp — the retired opencode tool suite is not part of it), the config.json shape, the SUPPORTED_COSANIMA version-string format, and the .trans/ data layout; everything else is out of scope for 1.0 stability (broadened per the user's ruling; the tool/agent-names item now resolves to the MCP surface per cosanima-mcp) [with user].

body: source/ruling: the binding architecture decision replaces the custom opencode tool-suite layer with a local MCP server (cosanima-mcp), and the MCP server + cross-harness agents are 1.0 deliverables. inconsistency: R6 + Decision D5 enumerated 'tool/agent names' in the stable surface, which previously read as the cosanima_* opencode tool names — but those tools are RETIRED, never shipped, so naming them as stable surface would commit 1.0 to a surface that does not exist. resolution: R6 and D5 now read the agent-facing stable surface as the MCP tool set + MCP resource names + the six agent names from cosanima-mcp; the retired opencode tool suite is explicitly excluded; D5's summary updated to match; parent now SpecDependsOn cosanima-mcp so the flag-day gate covers the MCP deliverable [with user].
